chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The best of vegetables is the endive (hinda'), and there is no leaf of it except that upon it is a drop from Paradise. So eat it and do not shake it off when eating it. He said: And my father (peace be upon him) forbade us from shaking it when we ate it.

key_terms.الْهِنْدَبَاءُ: Endive, a type of leafy green vegetable
key_terms.قَطْرَةٌ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ: A drop from Paradise, referring to the dew on the leaves

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of eating endive (hinda') according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the medicinal and spiritual virtues of endive (hinda'), portraying it as a blessed provision where each leaf retains a drop of Paradise's dew. The specific instruction not to shake off the dew reflects the Ahl al-Bayt's emphasis on preserving the natural purity and blessings of food, a practice consistently observed by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) and his father, Imam al-Baqir (AS).
